title: Pooled-Volume Tier Reviews of the Contingency Placement Agreements
content:
The tier of an agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements is reviewed against the client's placement volume, and tier reviews pool the client's whole portfolio.

## 1. Pooled trailing placement volume

The trailing placement volume used at a review is the sum of the placed balances of the placed accounts whose placement date falls in the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the review date, both ends included, across every agreement the client holds — not only the agreement under review.

## 2. When a review takes place

1. A tier review takes place only when the handling date is on or after the review date counted from the agreement's effective date.
2. Reviews fall every review-interval number of calendar months (the tier's review interval) after the effective date. A review date that does not exist in a short month falls on that month's last day.
3. The agreement's recorded next review date always records the next review.
4. The comparison is inclusive: a handling date equal to the review date satisfies it; a handling date before it does not.

## 3. Which agreements may change tier

Tiers are changed only on agreements whose status is active or placement hold; an agreement in runoff keeps its tier to the end. The status is read from the agreement record.

## 4. Movement at review

- The agreement moves up to the highest tier whose entry volume the pooled trailing volume meets.
- It moves down only when the pooled volume is more than the current tier's downgrade tolerance percent below the current tier's entry volume, in which case it moves to the highest tier whose entry volume is met.
- The new tier's contingency rates apply to collections received from the day after the review; collections already booked keep the rate applied when they were booked.

The review interval and the downgrade tolerance are the tier figures of the agreement's current tier; the entry volumes are those of the tier ladder.

## Hypothetical boundary cases

*Review date.* An agreement with an effective date of 29 February and a review interval of 12 months has its first review on 28 February of the following year, since that February has no 29th. A handling date of 28 February satisfies the review gate; a handling date of 27 February does not.

*Downgrade.* An agreement on a tier with an entry volume of 250000.00 USD and a downgrade tolerance of 10.0 percent:

| Pooled trailing volume (USD) | More than 10.0 percent below 250000.00? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 230000.00 | no | no downgrade; no higher tier's entry volume is met, so the tier is unchanged |
| 225000.00 | no (exactly 10.0 percent below) | tier unchanged |
| 224999.00 | yes | moves to the highest tier whose entry volume 224999.00 USD meets |

*Status.* The same downgrade figures on an agreement in runoff produce no tier change, because an agreement in runoff keeps its tier to the end.
